newsitem.title: USA: U.S. help-wanted ad index fell to 85 in December.
newsitem.headline: U.S. help-wanted ad index fell to 85 in December.

text.p: The U.S. help-wanted advertising index fell to 85.0 in December from a revised 87.0 in November, the Conference Board said on Thursday.
In the last three months, the volume of help-wanted advertising increased in five of the nine U.S. regions. The greatest increases were in the West North Central and Mountain regions.
The Conference Board said job advertising volume fell most sharply in the Middle Atlantic region, followed by New England.

"The labor market remains very healthy," said Conference Board economist Ken Goldstein. He said the economy was generating new jobs at a 2.0 percent annual rate at the end of 1996, and theinitial unemployment claims "were slowly moderating."
"All this data suggests that labor demand is not diminishing," he said.

The Conference Board report said want ad volume has remained in a range of about 85 to 90 throughout 1995 and 1996, which has generated an average of 230,000 net jobs per month during the two-year period.
The pace of job growth will not subside in the early months of 1997, according to Goldstein. He said sustained job growth and some rise in hourly compensation is reinforcing high consumer confidence.
"Job and income growth, associated with a high level of household optimism, could translate to strong consumer spending through the first half of 1997," he said.
